title: stale-node-drain-propagation-triggered-multitier-fallbacks-postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-01-27 we observed a rapid spike in cross-region and cross-tier fallbacks for hosted customers in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. The spike correlated with a rolling node drain that did not propagate 'drain complete' state for a subset of allocator nodes, causing the smart-routing controller to treat capacity as available in drained nodes and continue routing traffic to them. Inflight requests timed out or failed transiently, triggering automatic fallback policies that routed large volumes to lower-tier model variants and other regions. This produced amplified load on fallback pools and a visible degradation in latency and cost for affected customers.

High-level impact: increased 99th percentile generation latency (from 1.2s to 4.8s for affected accounts), fallback rate increased ~8x for a 45-minute window, and an observable cost uplift due to cross-region egress and lower-quantized variants being invoked more frequently. Several SLA-monitored customers experienced degraded latency and one customer reported errors in production flows.

This document captures the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and long-term fixes we implemented or scheduled.
impact_summary: 45-minute incident with 8x fallback rate spike; p99 latency doubled for affected traffic; cross-region egress increased monthly cost estimate for the day by ~14%; two enterprise customers reported degraded user-facing latency and opened support tickets.
timeline: 2025-01-27T11:03Z - Canary drain started in eu-west-1 for allocator pool eu-a scheduled as part of routine maintenance (autoscaler rotation).
2025-01-27T11:09Z - Monitoring alerted: small increase in request retries, routing controller logged WARN about stale capacity hints for allocator eu-a-2.

2025-01-27T11:12Z - Heartbeat gap observed from eu-a-2; drain controller attempted graceful drain and posted drain tombstone in coordination service. Tombstone write succeeded but tombstone TTL mis-set (extremely long) in 40% of cases due to edge case in tombstone-ttl calculation code.

2025-01-27T11:14Z - Smart routing cache continued to read allocator eu-a-2 as 'available' because tombstone TTL > expected and our reconciler skipped tombstone expiration checks for entries it considered 'recent'.
2025-01-27T11:20Z - Clients routed traffic to eu-a-2; requests began to queue on GPU hosts undergoing drain leading to intermittent timeouts at the serving runtime.

2025-01-27T11:26Z - Automatic fallback policy triggered: requests failing to meet latency SLOs were routed to fallback variants (lower-capacity quantized models) and remote regions (us-east-1). Fallback surge amplified load on fallback pools.
2025-01-27T11:35Z - Observability showed cascading effect: fallback-induced overloads created secondary cross-region drains as overloaded pools started to shed capacity.
2025-01-27T11:40Z - Incident declared. On-call SRE and routing team began mitigation.

2025-01-27T11:48Z - Emergency mitigation #1: temporarily increased conservative drain TTL checks in smart-routing reconciler and forced immediate tombstone expiry for eu-a-2 entries. This removed eu-a-2 from routing map for new requests.
2025-01-27T12:05Z - Emergency mitigation #2: raised fallback circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent aggressive cross-region fallbacks for 15 minutes, allowing overloaded fallback pools to recover.
2025-01-27T12:28Z - Traffic stabilized; fallback rate returned near baseline by ~12:45Z.
2025-01-27T12:50Z - Incident declared mitigated; post-incident review scheduled.
root_cause: Incorrect tombstone TTL calculation in drain controller: a float-to-int cast bug produced TTLs that were orders of magnitude longer when the node metadata path contained unexpected nil values.
Smart-routing reconciler optimization skipped TTL-expiry checks for allocators marked as 'recently updated', making the system blind to the erroneous long TTL in a subset of heap entries.

Fallback policy had insufficient guardrails (circuit-breakers) against simultaneous cross-region and cross-tier failover when multiple hosts in a priority pool enter degraded state. The policy assumes failing hosts are rare and independent.
mitigation_short_term: Forced tombstone expiry for affected allocators and restarted drain-controller on eu-west-1 nodes to clear stale state.
Tweaked smart-routing reconciler to always validate tombstone 'expiry_timestamp' value and to re-evaluate entries with TTLs outside expected bounds, regardless of 'recent' optimization flag.
Temporarily increased fallback circuit-breaker thresholds and applied emergency rate-limiting for cross-region fallback routing for 15 minutes while recovery completed.
Opened high-priority support communications with impacted customers and offered dedicated assist sessions.
mitigation_long_term: Fix tombstone TTL calculation and add unit+fuzz tests covering absent metadata and extreme numeric edge-cases (assigned to ENG-31410).
Refactor smart-routing reconciler to decouple 'recently-updated' optimization from TTL validation path; add integration tests that simulate drains and tombstone races (assigned to ENG-31602).

Enhance fallback policy with multi-dimensional circuit-breakers: combine region-level capacity signals, per-variant capacity headroom, and progressive backoffs to avoid amplification (design doc: CONFLUENCE-RT-439).
Add a safety network policy that can temporarily quarantine anomalous allocator nodes from routing decisions until explicit health verification is completed.
Create a canary playbook for drain rotations that includes preflight checks for tombstone TTLs and reconciler state validation (runbook: runbooks/drain-canary.md).
follow_up_actions: ENG-31410 - Fix TTL calc + add unit & fuzz tests (owner: Priya Menon) - due 2025-02-11
ENG-31602 - Reconciler refactor + integration tests (owner: Daniel Kim) - due 2025-03-02
PM-789 - Prioritize fallback policy redesign on roadmap and coordinate a spike to evaluate actuator-based circuit-breakers (owner: Maria Gonzalez) - cycle 2025-W07
Create an SLO alert that triggers when fallback rate > 3x baseline for 10m and notify routing-oncall + product-obs channel (owner: SRE team) - done
Run a DRILL: simulate simultaneous drains across two regions during next quarterly chaos window and validate fallback amplification mitigations (owner: Reliability squad) - scheduled 2025-03-20
